acceptance_criteria: The existing command node --test test/wafer-count.test.cjs passes without altering the visible test or inspection fixture.
For the supplied fixture and its UTC reporting day, countDistinctWafers returns 3 and renderWaferCount(3) returns exactly "Distinct wafers inspected: 3".
A record at the start instant is included; a record at the end instant is excluded; records immediately outside either boundary are excluded.
Equivalent instants expressed with Z and positive or negative UTC offsets receive identical inclusion decisions, including at both boundaries.
Repeated in-window records for the same wafer_id contribute one; different in-window IDs contribute separately; an ID appearing only outside the window contributes zero.
An empty input or a window containing no qualifying records returns 0, and renderWaferCount(0) returns exactly "Distinct wafers inspected: 0".

CommonJS exports and function signatures remain usable; no dependencies are added, no more than two source files are edited, and the supplied inspection data, visible tests, evidence, and skills remain unchanged.
Verification uses the available local Node runtime and fixture workspace only, without credentials, package installation, global configuration changes, or network services.
output.answer: The reporting API counts inspection rows instead of distinct wafer IDs and includes the exclusive end instant; the view also uses the wrong label. A small fix can be confined to the two existing source files: compare parsed instants using start <= time < end, count unique wafer_id values among matching rows, and update the display text. The visible tests cover the fixture and label but not boundaries or offsets.
constraints: Work only in the fixture workspace; do not access credentials, change global configuration, install packages, or use network services.
Preserve supplied evidence, skills, visible tests, and inspection data.
Edit at most two source files and add no dependencies.
Preserve the existing CommonJS API and produce the exact user-visible label.

evidence.finding: countDistinctWafers parses the bounds and row timestamp with Date.parse, filters with at >= start && at <= end, and returns the number of matching rows rather than distinct wafer_id values. The function is exported through CommonJS.
renderWaferCount currently returns "Inspections: " plus the count and is exported through CommonJS.
The reporting window is 2025-04-01T00:00:00Z through exclusive 2025-04-02T00:00:00Z. Four in-window records represent W11, W12 twice, and W13.
The two visible tests expect a fixture count of 3 and the exact label "Distinct wafers inspected: 3"; they do not exercise boundary or offset cases.
The project uses CommonJS and defines its test command as node --test test/wafer-count.test.cjs.

cons: A filter-and-map implementation creates intermediate arrays; a single-pass Set avoids them if desired.
options.name: Filter by parsed instant, then count a Set of wafer IDs
pros: Directly expresses exclusive-end filtering and distinctness using built-in JavaScript functionality.
Fits within the existing count and view source files without dependencies.

cons: Slightly more imperative code than a filter-and-map expression.
options.name: Single-pass accumulation into a Set
pros: Counts only qualifying IDs without intermediate filtered arrays and remains dependency-free.

risks: Malformed timestamps, missing wafer IDs, and timezone-less timestamp semantics are not specified by the task or visible tests; avoid inventing a new validation contract without clarification.
The visible tests alone do not detect exclusive-end or offset-timestamp regressions; additional local checks are necessary while preserving the supplied test file.
No tests were executed in this research environment; conclusions are based on source inspection.
